The promise closes at web:Isa.14.2 with the nations' captivity reversed, before the temporal frame that reopens the unit toward the king-of-Babylon mashal at web:Isa.14.3.

Yet the row ships the signal key oracle_frame.addressee_shift_restoration_promise and calls Jacob 'a fresh addressee' while itself stating he is the object of both verbs — a verbal object is not an addressee. The first explicit second person in this stretch stands one verse later: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.14.3, collate: byte), the next row's onset, not this seam. readjudication.grounds: Opening seam web:Isa.14.2|web:Isa.14.3, both sides re-derived. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.14.2, byte tier) is third-person narration to its last token — a 2nd-person suffix scan of oshb:Isa.14.1-14.2 returns 0 hits — with no ruled close device; the staged parashah inventory records SAMEKH at Isa.14.2 (single witness, tier-3). RIGHT (the row's own opening verse): וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier) is a verse-initial temporal-formula onset (skeleton class of the 'and it shall be in the day' opener: 14 verses book-wide, this the one non-'that day' member) that turns to direct second-person address inside the same clause — the scan of oshb:Isa.14.3 returns exactly four 2nd-person suffixes: the final token of וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔, both tokens of מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ, and the final token of אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ (all byte tier), against 0 in the two preceding verses. Two ruled tier-1 signals (formula onset, addressee shift) stand in the seam verse's own bytes: the seam is sound, and the finding says so. The defect is engagement, and it re-verifies field by field: boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.14.3 but no oshb:Isa.14.3; the rationale splices nothing from 14:3 and opens its Hebrew engagement at וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ (oshb:Isa.14.4, byte tier) — a 2ms verb, so the second-person frame IS byte-engaged one verse in, which is why this is engagement-class and not a missing warrant; device_notes and the signal key narrative_frame.direct_second_person_taunt rest the seam on 'the shift into direct second-person address at Isa.14.3' asserted from the WEB sentence alone; confidence ships high. Under the engagement standard (pointed splices plus tier labels mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim) a high-confidence row whose seam-verse warrant is engaged only in the translation is exactly the class the finding names. One further byte fact for the repair to disclose rather than fear: the rest-verb root recurs across this seam, וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier) and הָנִ֤יחַ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier), a skeleton-substring match (sweep: 4 verses skeleton) beside the eved-root echo the preceding row already discloses — root-level cross-seam cohesion that the addressee shift and formula onset outweigh, but which the cross-seam law asks to be named. Medium confirmed; cure as proposed (add oshb:Isa.14.3, splice its second-person cluster at byte tier, re-test the high confidence), no span change.

The dated burden runs through the Philistia taunt to its close at web:Isa.14.32, before the Moab header reopens the series at web:Isa.15.1.

The boundary is not shown wrong — the PE at MT 14:27 (pmarks inventory, single-witness tier-3) and the second-person Philistia address opening oshb:Isa.14.29 (byte read) support the forward reading — so the defect is the undisclosed rival and the ungrounded direction claim: medium confirmed.

readjudication.grounds: Opening seam web:Isa.14.27|web:Isa.14.28, both sides re-derived. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): the oath oracle opened by נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.14.24, byte tier) closes on a rhetorical-question pair ending וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה וּֽמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה (oshb:Isa.14.27, byte tier) — no ruled close device; its stretched-hand wording is a DIFFERENT object from the five-site refrain (sweep: the articular 'his hand, the stretched-out one' skeleton stands at 1 verse, oshb:Isa.14.27; the refrain skeleton at 5 verses, oshb:Isa.5.25, 9.11, 9.16, 9.20, 10.4 = web:Isa.5.25, 9.12, 9.17, 9.21, 10.4), never blended; the staged parashah inventory records PE at Isa.14.27 (single witness, tier-3). RIGHT (the row's own opening verse): בִּשְׁנַת מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.14.28, byte tier, the whole verse) opens on the regnal dating formula בִּשְׁנַת מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ, which recurs with בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ at oshb:Isa.6.1 (byte tier) — sweep: 1 verse byte, 2 accent_stripped, 2 skeleton — where the same frame opens the throne-vision unit; a date-frame onset explicit in the bytes is a ruled frame-onset class, so the seam is warranted from the right whichever way the demonstrative points, and the strategy's inventory classes the mid-verse token as a header REFERENCE (the massa role split), which aligns with the forward reading without ruling the direction. That is why the boundary is not shown wrong. The finding's defect stands on the complete test: the verse ends הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.14.28, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse skeleton for the phrase), an anaphoric-capable demonstrative with nothing else in the verse fixing direction, and the backward construal is structurally viable — on it oshb:Isa.14.28 is a dated colophon closing the oath oracle and this row would open at אַֽל תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י פְלֶ֨שֶׁת֙ כֻּלֵּ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.14.29, byte tier), a vocative-plus-prohibitive summons that is itself a ruled tier-1 onset (imperative/vocative class, 2fs address to Philistia), with the Moab header מַשָּׂ֖א מוֹאָ֑ב at oshb:Isa.15.1 (byte tier) unaffected. The row asserts 'pointing forward' flatly in two fields, its single rejected-alternative sentence disposes only of the form question (mid-verse reference versus the ten verse-initial headers), and the mandated rival-disclosure slot is unused. An undisclosed rival construal at a load-bearing left edge, with byte support on both sides of the question and the boundary itself sound: medium confirmed; cure as proposed (add the rival sentence naming the backward construal and the byte ground for setting it aside — the accent_stripped recurrence of the date frame with the unit-opening oshb:Isa.6.1 and the header-reference role are grounds the row can hold), no span change.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This chapter is a single sign-act report bounded by its own narrative onset, “In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod” (web:Isa.20.1), and the command frame "בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ" (oshb:Isa.20.2, byte tier) -- a time-frame and messenger clause continuing, in the same verse, into an imperative to strip off sackcloth and sandals and the compliance clause reporting it done, “He did so, walking naked and barefoot.” (web:Isa.20.2). The interpretation opens with its own divine-speech onset, "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), “Yahweh said,” (web:Isa.20.3); the servant reference naming the sign-actor is explicit rather than one of the unnamed servant-figure zones elsewhere in the book: "עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ" (oshb:Isa.20.3, byte tier), "my servant Isaiah," names the prophet himself, “As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,” (web:Isa.20.3). Although narrated in the third person from start to finish rather than as a first-person report, the whole chapter is held as one row bounded by the sign-act's own narrative frame: the divine-speech onset at Isa.20.3 does not open a fresh narrative episode but supplies that same episode's own explanation of the sign already performed and completed in Isa.20.2, and no new narrative-onset marker -- a fresh time-frame or scene turn -- recurs to divide it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this unit as narrative_prose parallel to the later court narrative is a defensible alternative label to vision_report, since the whole account is third-person past-tense narration of a sign-act rather than a first-person vision report; the operative-category deviation is disclosed here rather than argued away.

A byte-false load-bearing closing-seam warrant: confirm at high.
